hints.title: Eulerian Trail Structure
hints.text: A continuous route chaining end-to-start pairs forms an Eulerian path on a directed multigraph.

hints.title: Degree Balance Start Node
hints.text: The start node must have out_degree minus in_degree equal to one, or any node with outgoing edges if all degrees balance.

hints.title: Hierholzer Path Construction
hints.text: Traverse edges exhaustively using a stack, appending exhausted vertices to the route and reversing at completion.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def validArrangement(self, pairs: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
        adj = defaultdict(list)
        in_degree = defaultdict(int)
        out_degree = defaultdict(int)

        for u, v in pairs:
            adj[u].append(v)
            out_degree[u] += 1
            in_degree[v] += 1

        start = pairs[0][0]
        for node in out_degree:
            if out_degree[node] - in_degree[node] == 1:
                start = node
                break

        route = []
        stack = [start]
        while stack:
            while adj[stack[-1]]:
                stack.append(adj[stack[-1]].pop())
            route.append(stack.pop())

        route.reverse()
        return [[route[i], route[i + 1]] for i in range(len(route) - 1)]
```

complexity.time: O(V + E) Hierholzer algorithm for Eulerian path
complexity.space: O(V + E) adjacency graph and path stack
complexity.notes: Find Eulerian path by locating node with out_degree - in_degree == 1, then post-order reconstruct edges.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple backtracking takes exponential time when traversing cyclic graph branches.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hierholzer algorithm visits each edge exactly once in linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize this as an Eulerian path problem and apply degree counting.
